title: Development of Microfluidic Devices to Study the Elongation Capability of Tip-growing Plant Cells in Extremely Small Spaces
protocol: Fabricate the PDMS microdevice to examine growing pollen tubes and moss protonemata.
Pour 11 g of pre-polymer PDMS mixture (elastomer base:curing agent at a ratio of 10:1) into each 4-inch mold.
Degas the mold for 20 min in a vacuum chamber.
Cure the mold at 65 °C for 90 min in a non-convection oven.
Peel the PDMS layer off the mold and punch access holes into the fluidic channels using biopsy punches.
Expose the PDMS layer and a glass bottom dish to air plasma for 50 s.
Press the PDMS layer into the glass bottom dish.
Heat at 65 °C for 30 min in a non-convection oven to completely seal off the microfluidic network.
Repeat steps 1.1 - 1.3 using molds to prepare two PDMS layers for the root and root hair microdevices.
Expose both PDMS layers to air plasma for 50 seconds.
Assemble the two PDMS layers under a stereomicroscope using a custom-made desktop aligner.
Ensure microchannels on both PDMS layers face each other during assembly.
Match alignment marks on both PDMS layers before assembling.
Heat assembled PDMS layers at 65 °C for 30 minutes in a non-convection oven to seal the microfluidic network.
Remove cover slip from the constructed microdevice and place it on a glass bottom dish that is 5 cm in diameter.
Prepare modified Nitsch's medium as described previously.
Autoclave the prepared medium at 121 °C for 20 minutes.

Mix NH4NO3 (80 mg/L), KNO3 (125 mg/L), Ca(NO3)2‧4H2O (500 mg/L), MgSO4‧7H2O (125 mg/L), KH2PO4 (125 mg/L), MnSO4‧4H2O (3 mg/L), ZnSO4‧7H2O (0.5 mg/L), H3BO3 (10 mg/L), CuSO4‧5H2O (0.025 mg/L), Na2MoO4‧2H2O (0.025 mg/L), sucrose (50,000 mg/L), and casein (500 mg/L) to prepare modified Nitsch's medium.
Store the prepared modified Nitsch's medium at 4 °C for up to 4 months.
Prepare a solution of polyethylene glycol at 26% (w/v) using autoclaved deionized water.
Filter the polyethylene glycol solution with a 0.3 µm pore filter.
Store filtered polyethylene glycol solution at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Mix modified Nitsch's medium and polyethylene glycol solution in a 1:1 (v/v) ratio.
Use freshly prepared mixture immediately for each experiment.
Prepare a solution of 0.215% (w/v) Murashige & Skoog Medium, 0.05% (w/v) MES, 1% (w/v) sucrose, and 1% (w/v) agar in deionized water.
Autoclave the solution at 121 °C for 20 min.
Pre-incubate moss protonemata in BCDAT medium in a Petri dish.
Culture the moss in BCDATG medium in the microdevice.
Place the pollen tube microdevice in a vacuum chamber and degas for 20 min.
Remove the microdevice from the vacuum chamber.
Introduce the growth medium to the pistil inlet using a micropipette with a very fine tip.
Fill remaining wells to their tops with the same medium.
Wait until all microchannels are filled with the medium by the vacuum created inside of the microchannels.
Place wet paper towel in the glass bottom dish to maintain humidity.
Transfer pollen grains from a wild-type T. fournieri 'blue and white' flower to its stigma using a dissection needle.
Cut the pollinated style (1 cm long) using a blade.
Insert the cut style into the inlet of the device as shown.
Put a lid on the dish and seal it with tape.
Place the device in an incubator at 28 °C for 5 - 6 h in darkness.
Sterilize seeds from A. thaliana Columbia (Col-0) by soaking them in sterile liquid (5% v/v household bleach and 0.02 % v/v Triton X-100) for 5 min.
Thoroughly rinse the sterilized seeds with autoclaved water.
Store the rinsed seeds in water for 2 days at 4 °C in darkness.
Sterilize the microdevice under UV light overnight.
Place the microdevice in a vacuum chamber and degas for 20 min.
Introduce the growth medium to the wells in the device using a micropipette.
Wait a few minutes until the vacuum fills all the microchannels with the medium.
Place autoclaved wet paper towel in the glass bottom dish to maintain the humidity in the dish.
Transfer a sterilized seed into the inlet of the device.
Put a lid on the dish and seal it with tape.
Place the device vertically in an incubator at 22 °C under continuous white light.
Check root hair growth after 4 - 10 days of incubation.
Obtain both bright field and fluorescent images using an inverted microscope.
Preculture P. patens strain Gransden 200418 on BCDAT medium covered with cellophane in a Petri dish for one week under continuous white light at 25 °C.
Sterilize the microdevice under UV light overnight in a laminar flow hood.
Place the microdevice in a vacuum chamber and degas for 20 min.
Introduce the growth medium to the wells using a micropipette.
Wait a few minutes until the vacuum fills all the microchannels with the medium.
Add autoclaved water into the dish surrounding the microdevice to maintain the humidity in the dish.
Transfer a small piece of moss protonemata tissue to the inlet of the microdevice.
Culture the tissue in an incubator at 25 °C under continuous white light.
Check the moss protonemata growth after 2 - 3 weeks of incubation.
Obtain bright field images using a microscope.
Place the microdevice on an inverted fluorescence microscope equipped with image acquisition hardware.
Find the microgap locations.
Capture bright field images every 10 seconds using microscope image acquisition software.
Irradiate the specimen with a 561 nm laser for fluorescent imaging.
Use a bandpass optical filter (578/105 nm) to observe the fluorescently labeled sperm cells and vegetative nucleus.
Adjust the brightness and contrast of the images using ImageJ software.
Prepare a video file using ImageJ software.
